newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel evicts bedouin to expand Jewish settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israel evicts bedouin to expand Jewish settlement.

text.p: Israeli police evicted on Wednesday the last group of Palestinian bedouin from their West Bank encampment to clear the way for expansion of a Jewish settlement, Israeli officials and witnesses said.

Witnesses said two Palestinians fainted and about 20 were detained when police dragged away young bedouin and some Israeli peace activists from a tin-shack encampment near Maaleh Adumim settlement east of Jerusalem.
"This is an action that has never happened in any country in the world," said Mohammed al-Hiresh, a leader of the Jahalin bedouin tribe.
Witnesses said African workers moved the bedouins' belongings from their shacks and tents before bulldozers levelled the encampment.
Israeli military authorities say the bedouin were squatting on state lands designated since 1981 for the expansion of Maaleh Adumim.

The bedouin say they have lived on the land since Israel forced them to leave their homes in the Negev desert in 1950 and drove them across the demarcation line to the then Jordanian-controlled West Bank.

Peter Lerner, spokesman for the Israeli military authorities Civil Administration, said a total of 90 bedouin were evicted on Wednesday. He said they were the last group to be expelled from the site since the Jahalin lost a legal battle in Israel's Supreme Court last September.
Israel evicted the rest of the Jahalin in three separate operations since the start of the year. Israeli peace activists condemned the move as "ethnic cleansing."

"Gush Shalom, the Israeli peace bloc, strongly condemns the continuing persecution of the Jahalin tribe by the government of Israel -- a despicable racist policy nothing less than a policy of ethnic cleansing," the group said in a statement.
Lerner said the Palestinians were being moved to a new site where each family would be allocated a small plot of land on a 25-year-lease.
Human rights organisations say the new site was located some 500 metres (555 yards) from a rubbish dump and would cause health hazards.
